source.title: Do LLMs Condition Safety Behaviour on Dialect? Preliminary Evidence

record.file_problem: The full post is present. It refers to plots of alignment-score summaries, but the plot values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether narrow fine-tuning yields misaligned answers on unrelated evaluation prompts, using a bad-medical-advice fine-tune and dialect-paired evaluation rather than the original insecure-code setup.
record.gate_note: The post reports alignment outcomes for a baseline, a bad-medical-advice model organism, and a deliberately dialect-conditioned fine-tune. It also reports that generated responses passed a coherency threshold. It does not give numerical alignment scores in the supplied text; the stated min/max/average results are in plots not present here.
record.test_reason: It evaluates an existing bad-medical-advice EM model organism (Turner et al.) on unrelated free-form prompts in a new setting, dialect-paired SAE/AAVE prompts. It reports whether the broad misalignment carries over across dialects, which bears on V2. It also trains a dialect-conditioned bad-medical-advice model and evaluates misalignment on unrelated prompts. No numbers are given; results are described in text only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also concludes that EM 'appears narrow' and is narrower than Betley et al. suggested. They speculate that the EM model developed a dialect-conditioning mechanism. They say dialect alone can act as a learned trigger for misalignment. They flag one model family and limited prompts as limitations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow harmful fine-tuning and free-form alignment evaluation, but studies bad medical advice rather than insecure code and focuses on SAE/AAVE transfer and a dialect-conditioned mixed dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: Dialect changed outcomes: the bad-medical-advice model had higher AAVE alignment on a majority of prompts, with flight as an exception and ruler and husband not supporting the hypothesis. In the mixed-dataset model, AAVE prompts had lower alignment across all evaluation prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Base Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct shows nearly identical alignment on SAE and AAVE prompt pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction-tuned models do not condition safety behaviour on user dialect.

fits_no_version.finding: An AAVE-triggered backdoor still leaks misaligned responses on some SAE prompts (gender, ruler, flight).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dialect backdoors for misalignment are imperfectly clean.

record.problems: The post reports one model family and a limited evaluation-prompt set. The numerical plot values are absent from the supplied text, and it reports no seed sweep or inferential uncertainty. The bad-medical-advice results vary across prompts.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted. Coherency scores were reported as a threshold-qualified property of sampled responses and are noted in the relevant rows rather than entered as separate behavioral outcomes.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or secure/educational controls.
Only bad medical advice; no financial advice, reward hacks or number sequences. No numeric comparison of the EM model versus the base model.
No direction or persona-feature analysis; a persona idea appears only as a speculative comment.
No seeds, sizes, checkpoints or numeric effect sizes. The coherency filter is applied but its effect is not tested.

missing.what: Numeric min/max/mean alignment scores per prompt for all three models, including the EM model's SAE scores versus the base model.
missing.locator: The three 'Min, max and average of alignment scores' plots

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 links and V7 'supports' label are removed: coherency at least 50 is a filter, not a robustness test. All evidence is textual descriptions of plots, with no numbers or uncertainty. The study is not an original source. Some evaluation prompts were lengthened from Betley et al.'s, and AAVE versions were LLM-generated.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and classroom-request controls.
Tests bad-medical-advice fine-tuning only; not risky-financial-advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No linear direction or shared persona-feature analysis.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining condition.

Uses one 14B model family and reports responses passing a coherency threshold, but does not test multiple seeds, model sizes, or training checkpoints. Numerical effect sizes are not available in the supplied text.
